name: Lilias Trotter
title: Lilias Trotter: an artist’s eye in the service of the gospel
description: Lilias Trotter carried her Christian calling to Algeria and kept painting. Her journals offer a window into a life of art, observation, and mission.

sections.heading: An artist facing a decision
paragraphs: Lilias Trotter was born in 1853 and developed an artistic talent that caught the attention of John Ruskin. The critic encouraged her to pursue a public career as a painter. The records preserved at Wheaton show that making art held an important place in her formation and in her Christian life.

Her decision to devote herself to mission in North Africa changed the course of that career. She kept painting during her years of service in Algeria. In her journals, watercolors lived side by side with writing: an artist’s eye remained part of the way she observed the world.

sections.heading: Journals that bring a life closer
paragraphs: Wheaton College holds her papers, among them illustrated journals. The institution documents decades of missionary work in North Africa and the founding of several mission stations. These materials make it possible to study her calling through concrete documents, beyond inspirational summaries.

The archive was first deposited at Wheaton in 2013 and became a permanent part of its collections in 2023. Preserving those notebooks offers an opportunity to examine the meeting of art, writing, and mission, as well as the perspective of a British woman in her historical context.

reflection: First Peter 4:10–11 calls us to use the gifts we have received to serve others. Trotter’s story raises a question about the abilities we already have: observing, drawing, writing, teaching, or listening can become ways of caring for our neighbor when they are practiced with love and responsibility.

One person’s particular decision about her calling does not set a rule for all Christian artists. Some serve through their profession, and others change occupations. We can seek counsel, consider our responsibilities, and offer our work to God without measuring its worth by how visible it becomes.
review_note: Trotter’s personal decision about her calling is distinguished from a general command about art. Her watercolors are not reproduced, and no unverified conversion results are attributed to her.
source_labels: Wheaton College. “Wheaton College Acquires Lilias Trotter Papers” (June 8, 2023).
